title.en: One word that joins mind and body

text.en: Every year on 21st June people across the world stretch, breathe and sit quietly together. That day is International Yoga Day. In this chapter you will learn what yoga is, how it helps us and how two tricky words, practice and practise, differ.

Think about what you know about yoga and what 21st June is known for. The class game of Antakshari with the word yoga helps collect yoga-related words: asana, breath, calm, stretch and so on. The chapter is an informational passage, so we read it to get facts and the main idea.
Yoga is a physical, mental and spiritual practice that started in ancient India. The word yoga comes from the Sanskrit root yuj, which means to join or to unite. It stands for unity of mind and body, of thought and action, and harmony between humans and nature. It is a holistic approach to health, meaning it looks after the whole person. Sage Patanjali set out the tradition in a systematic way in the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, describing yoga as a way to make the mind quiet and free from distractions.
Asanas, or postures, stretch and strengthen muscles and improve flexibility, endurance and balance. This improves overall fitness and can reduce body pain such as lower back pain. Breathing techniques and meditation calm the mind, reduce stress and anxiety, improve sleep and increase concentration. Yoga can boost the immune system, improve heart health by lowering blood pressure and improving circulation, and help in weight loss by burning calories. Yoga gives a sense of overall well-being, and this is why its benefits are recognised across the world.
On 20 June 2021 the World Health Organisation launched an app called WHO mYoga, with videos and audio files to teach and support yoga practice. The aim was an easy-to-use, free tool for people everywhere. This shows how important yoga is for health across the world. On 11 December 2014 the United Nations General Assembly accepted the proposal to celebrate 21 June as International Yoga Day. Seals of the Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation, dating to about 2700 BC, suggest that yoga was known in ancient India.
We can start yoga at any moment. When we practise asanas we do not only stretch the body, since the mind has to be with the body too. So it should be done without distractions. If each stretch is joined with breath and awareness, our practice becomes a yogic practice. An old verse from the Hatha Yoga Pradipika says that asana comes first and is practised for a steady posture, health and lightness of the body.
Practice with c is a noun. It means the actual use or exercise of a skill, as in a regular practice of stretching or a lot of practice to improve. Practise with s is a verb. It means doing something again and again to improve, as in I practise yoga every day. The same pattern works for advice and advise: advice with c is the noun, as in good advice, and advise with s is the verb, as in the doctor will advise rest. Tip: noun has c, verb has s, just as in the alphabet n comes before v, and c comes before s.
Make words from the letters R Y E N A G O, using the letter A in each word. Good examples are orange, anger, organ, range, gear and near. In speaking, share your yoga thoughts. If you have tried yoga say what you like. If not, say what you wish to try. Write a paragraph called The Benefits of Yoga with an opening line, supporting ideas and a concluding line. The sentence starters are: yoga is important because, one benefit is, and yoga is not just physical exercise. The listening passage tells of a girl whose grandfather, who is 65, practises yoga and is fit. She does breathing exercises to feel calm and focused before competitions.

problem.en: Choose practice or practise: I ____ yoga every day to keep my mind and body healthy.

text.en: Ask whether the missing word is an action or a thing.

why.en: The sentence needs an action, so a verb.

text.en: Verb uses s, so the answer is practise.

why.en: Practice with c is the noun.

problem.en: Choose practice or practise: The teacher said this needs a lot of ____ to improve.

text.en: Here the missing word is a thing, something you do a lot of.
Noun uses c, so the answer is practice.

prompt.en: Explain the idea of unity in yoga and two ways yoga helps people.

requiredIdeas.en: Yoga comes from yuj, to join.
It unites mind and body, thought and action and humans with nature.
It stretches muscles and increases flexibility.
It calms the mind, reduces stress and improves sleep.

commonMisconceptions.en: Yoga started in the twentieth century.

points.en: Yoga is a physical, mental and spiritual practice from ancient India.
The word yoga means to join or unite.
It improves strength, flexibility, sleep, concentration and heart health.
21 June is celebrated as International Yoga Day.
Practice is a noun; practise is a verb; advice is a noun; advise is a verb.
